A pterodactyl is a type of flying reptile that lived millions of years ago and is now completely extinct. Think of it like a giant lizard with wings — something like a dragon, but real.

What exactly is it?

A pterodactyl is a prehistoric flying reptile that soared through the skies during the age of dinosaurs. It had large wings, a long beak (often filled with teeth), and clawed limbs. It was a real, living creature — not a myth — and fossils of it have been found all over the world.

The wings were not made of feathers like a bird's wings. Instead, they were made of a thin, leathery skin membrane — like a bat's wings — stretched across an extremely long finger bone and attached to the body. This membrane was tough but lightweight, allowing the animal to fly.

Was it a dinosaur?

This is one of the most common misunderstandings about this word, and it is important to get it right.

No. A pterodactyl was not a dinosaur. It lived alongside dinosaurs during the same era, but it belonged to a completely separate group of animals called pterosaurs (flying reptiles). Dinosaurs, by scientific definition, were land animals. Pterodactyls ruled the skies while dinosaurs ruled the land, and different creatures ruled the seas.

Everyday use vs. Scientific use

The word "pterodactyl" is actually used in two slightly different ways, and knowing both will help you understand it completely:

1. In everyday/casual language, people use "pterodactyl" loosely to mean any large, flying prehistoric reptile. When someone in a movie, a book, or a cartoon says "pterodactyl," they usually just mean one of those big, winged, ancient flying creatures in general.

2. In science, "pterodactyl" refers more precisely to a specific genus (a scientific grouping) called Pterodactylus — a relatively small flying reptile, roughly the size of a seagull, that lived about 150 million years ago during the Jurassic period.

Here's where it gets interesting: the large, iconic flying reptile that most people picture when they hear "pterodactyl" — the one with a huge crest on its head and a wingspan as wide as a car — is actually a different animal called a Pteranodon. Pteranodon was much bigger, lived during the Cretaceous period, and had no teeth (unlike the true Pterodactylus). But because people use "pterodactyl" loosely, these two creatures get mixed up all the time.

So when you hear the word in everyday life, it generally just means a big flying reptile from the age of dinosaurs. In a scientific context, it means that one specific, smaller creature.

What were they like?

  • Size: Pterodactyls varied enormously. Some were as small as a sparrow. Others, like the giant Quetzalcoatlus, had wingspans of up to 10–11 meters (roughly 35 feet) — wider than a school bus is long — making them among the largest flying animals that ever existed.
  • Diet: Many pterodactyls ate fish, scooping them from the water with their long beaks. Others ate insects or small animals.
  • Flight: They were likely strong fliers and could soar on air currents, similar to how large birds like eagles and albatrosses fly today.
  • Bone structure: Their bones were hollow and lightweight, much like modern birds, which helped keep them light enough to fly despite sometimes being enormous.
  • Crests: Many species had distinctive bony crests on their heads. Scientists believe these may have been used for attracting mates or regulating body heat.

When did they live, and what happened to them?

Pterodactyls (and all pterosaurs) lived during the Mesozoic Era, which spans three periods:

  • The Triassic (when pterosaurs first appeared, about 228 million years ago)
  • The Jurassic (when they flourished)
  • The Cretaceous (when the most famous large ones, like Pteranodon, lived)

They went extinct approximately 66 million years ago, at the same time as the non-bird dinosaurs, almost certainly due to the catastrophic asteroid impact that dramatically changed Earth's climate and wiped out a massive proportion of life on the planet.

How is the word used in a sentence?

  • "The museum had a complete skeleton of a pterodactyl hanging from the ceiling."
  • "In the film, the explorers were attacked by a flock of pterodactyls swooping down from the cliffs."
  • "Pterodactyls were not dinosaurs, though they lived during the same era."
  • "She let out a scream so loud and sharp that her friends jokingly called it a pterodactyl screech." (a humorous, informal use — high-pitched and prehistoric-sounding!)

The One-Line Summary

A pterodactyl is an extinct, winged reptile — not a dinosaur — that flew through prehistoric skies millions of years ago, with leathery wings, a long beak, and in some species, an enormous size that made it the largest flying creature to ever exist on Earth.
